Chase the sweet bokkia noodles buried under shaved ice at Bokkia Tha Din Daeng in Bangkok, the three-flavor Thai custard at Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai in Ayutthaya, or charcoal-griddled roti dipped in beef massaman at Roti Chaofa in Phuket. Old recipes, made fresh, worth every baht.

faq.q: Which one should I try first?
faq.a: Start with Bokkia Tha Din Daeng in Bangkok for its signature sweet bokkia: wheat noodles buried under shaved ice, drizzled with light syrup, with toppings you pick yourself. It is a hard-to-find cold treat and the reason people line up.

faq.q: Where do I go for a classic Thai sweet?
faq.a: Head to Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai in Ayutthaya for its little chicken-brand cups of baked custard in three flavors: egg, mung bean, and taro. Rich and just-sweet-enough, and easy to take home as a gift.

faq.q: I want roti in Phuket. Which shop?
faq.a: You have two Bib picks. Roti Chaofa griddles its roti over charcoal and serves it with beef massaman for dipping, while Roti Thaew Nam pairs its roti with a beef curry. Both are worth the stop.

faq.q: Are there filling savory options here?
faq.a: Yes. Khao Mun Gai Nha Jone in Pathum Thani does chicken rice with juicy thigh meat and a punchy dipping sauce, Dan Chicken Rice in Chiang Mai comes with a house ginger sauce, and Pae Brass Pot Porridge in Bangkok serves pork congee with egg simmered in a brass pot for 38 years running.
Most of these are walk-in small-eats counters, so no booking needed. Just go early or skip peak hours, since Bib favorites like Pae Brass Pot Porridge and Bokkia Tha Din Daeng draw steady crowds.
